title: Lawvere Fixed-Point Theorem for Setoids (CCC Generalization)

problemStatement.formal: \text{If } (Y, \approx) \text{ is a setoid and } \text{decode}(\text{encode}(f))(y) \approx f(y) \text{ for all } f, y, \text{ then } \forall f : Y \to Y, \exists p : Y, f(p) \approx p
problemStatement.plain: Lawvere fixed-point theorem generalized from exact Type equality to setoid equivalence. The diagonal construction works unchanged; the retraction need only hold up to setoid equivalence.

insights: The diagonal construction g(y) = f(decode(y)(y)) works unchanged in the setoid setting
f need NOT be a setoid morphism — fixed point exists for all f : Y → Y
Discrete setoid recovers the Type-level theorem exactly (type reduction to special case)
Setoid framework models CCC equality-up-to-isomorphism within Lean type theory
Retraction condition decode(encode(g))(y) ≈ g(y) (pointwise setoid) is the correct weakening

S2 — the trivial (one-class) setoid always admits coding vacuously: choose any constant encode and id-decode; ≈ ≡ True absorbs the retract. So Bool *can* code its endomorphisms — it just depends on the setoid choice.

S2 — coding-existence is monotone-DOWNWARD in the refinement lattice on Setoid Y: finer setoid admits coding ⇒ every coarser one does too (same encode/decode, weaker retract). So discrete-setoid coding is the strongest form, trivial-setoid coding the weakest.

S2 — the discrete and trivial setoids bracket the full coding spectrum: between them lie the interesting setoids (parity, congruence classes, isomorphism-up-to-coherence) where coding-feasibility carries genuine information.

S2 — counterexample direction: knowing Bool cannot code under discrete (S1) does *not* preclude coding under coarser setoids. Conversely, knowing Bool codes under trivial (S2) does *not* lift to finer setoids. The refinement structure is the right organizing principle for OQ-04-OQ-01-OQ-02 (characterization).
